items.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
items.q: you take Glenn Miller and his fine arrangements, he used to carry a dissonant interval sometimes.

ctx.x: Well, he didn't play the clarinet out of tune as he did the soprano. Or you didn't notice it? No. I didn't know it. To me, he's just a natural kind of player. Just natural.

But the old soprano, I just never did it. Maybe it wasn't out of tune, but I just didn't like the old tone of it. To me, it wasn't a good tone. But what I call good tone, lots of other people, they like something that's a little, they call it a little weird or something. Just a little kind of off color. I guess there's something to it, because now, you take Glenn Miller and his fine arrangements, he used to carry a dissonant interval sometimes. It's all fine. But of course, those guys are all in tune. They had to…
Did the New Orleans men impress you with their improvisation? Because they worked more as improvisational musicians, didn't they then?
